A5_counterexample.conclusion: C5 (hence A5) is not an isometry of the locked metric

attempts.reason: The locked metric is not rotationally invariant.  Its exact isometry group is the discrete cyclic group C4.  That group is not the Standard Model gauge group.  Identifying C4 with a residual discrete symmetry is possible but is not a derivation of SU(3)×SU(2)×U(1).

attempts.attempt: three generations from the APS index on the truncated conoid
attempts.verdict: failed for the untwisted Dirac operator
attempts.untwisted_status: theorem: index = 0 (bounding spin structure at both ends)
attempts.partial_route: The Falomir disk index equals 3 if an auxiliary U(1) flux satisfies κ ∈ (2, 3].  That κ is not determined by the locked metric (the spin connection is already included in the untwisted Dirac operator).
attempts.reason: Product-collar APS + vanishing 2D Â-genus give index 0 for the bounding spin structure, independently of the cut radii and of ℓ₀.  Index 3 is possible only with an extra flux or a finite spectral triple that already contains three summands; neither is derived here.

attempts.attempt: SM mass ratios from exact E0(m) ratios
attempts.reason: The ratios E0(m)/E0(n) are exact and cutoff-independent, but they are O(1) numbers (about 1.61, 2.75, 4.19, …).  The charged-lepton mass ratios are two to three orders of magnitude larger.  No identification of channel index m with a generation is made, and no match is claimed.

attempts.attempt: unique geometric derivation of omega0 and the 4/13 exponent
attempts.reason: No dimensionless quantity built from (C0, C4, ℓ₀-free ratios, ξ_∞, channel-energy ratios, or standard constants) equals ω₀ = e^{-4/π²/√e} or produces the exponent 4/13 uniquely.  Both remain free inputs of the Dual-Zero generator.

attempts.attempt: unique spectral-action derivation of the G_N prefactor α
attempts.rewrite_with_exact_C0: If one writes the Einstein–Hilbert coefficient in terms of the exact finite part C0 = 2π ln 2 and a cutoff moment φ2, then α = 1 / (c * φ2 * C0) for a conventional factor c (e.g. 16π or 32π²).  The exact C0 removes one numerical uncertainty but does not remove the scheme dependence in φ2 or in c.
attempts.reason: Different admissible cutoff moments and volume identifications produce different α, already visible in the scheme table.  The conventional value 64π/45 is a choice of scheme, not a uniqueness theorem.

attempts.attempt: gauge-coupling unification from the spectral action on conoid × F
attempts.reason: The bosonic spectral action yields Yang–Mills terms whose coefficients depend on (i) the cutoff moments of the action and (ii) the traces / KO-dimension data of a finite spectral triple F.  F is not derived from the locked conoid, and the cutoff moments are the same scheme data that leave α in G_N unfixed.  Without those inputs there is no honest unification prediction (no unique g1:g2:g3 or unique MU).
